1. **The idea.** Whether buying or renting-and-investing comes out ahead after ten years depends on one assumption: the return the renter earns on the invested money. The scene shows a row of small houses beside an apartment building with a "RENT" sign that shows an assumed return rate. A house window is lit if the buyer is ahead after ten years. It is dark if the renter's pile is bigger. The banner marks it "ILLUSTRATIVE" and cites FHFA, BLS, Freddie Mac and K. R. French (CRSP) as data sources.

2. **What changes.** The number on the RENT sign changes: 5%, then 5.1%, 4.83%, 5.59%, 5.59%, and back to 5%. The caption changes with it. It starts at "5%: about half lit," then becomes "flip point: about 5.1%." From frame 4 on it adds "Census range: 4.83% to 5.59% a year · 47.2% to 58.3% lit." The houses look much the same from frame to frame. The legible change is the sign and the text. I can't tell from the stills how many windows are lit in each frame.

3. **What it means.** At an assumed return of about 5%, the outcome is close to a toss-up, with roughly half the historical cases favoring the buyer. About 5.1% is the point where the two options break even. If the assumed return is lower (4.83%), more cases favor the buyer. If it is higher (5.59%), more favor the renter. Across that range, the share of buyer-ahead cases runs from 47.2% to 58.3%. The result is therefore very sensitive to the return you assume. The footer says "US only · history, not a forecast." Frame 6 has a faint line, "the tag is an assumption," which says the sign's number is an assumed input.

4. **Advice a viewer would take.** The image gives no direct advice. A viewer would probably come away with the message that "rent and invest the difference" is not a sure win. It is roughly a coin flip, and it depends on the return you assume. That is a takeaway about the evidence, not an instruction to buy or to rent.

5. **Source of the conclusion.** The animation itself suggests this takeaway, through the on-screen text. That text includes "flip point," "history, not a forecast," "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "the tag is an assumption." The cautionary reading, that the result is sensitive and not guaranteed, comes from those words. I added no advice of my own beyond describing that takeaway.
